newsitem.title: BELGIUM: AIRLINES, EU IN OZONE MEASURING PROJECT - SABENA.
newsitem.headline: AIRLINES, EU IN OZONE MEASURING PROJECT - SABENA.

text.p: Four European airlines are starting a project to measure levels of ozone during flights to assess the impact of pollution on the environment.

Belgian airline Sabena -- one of the participating carriers -- on Monday said the Mozaic project would study the effect of industry in general as well as aviation in particular on the climate, public health and flora.

Half of the cost of Mozaic, or Measurement of OZone by Airbus In-service airCraft, will be borne by the European Union, while the Airbus consortium, the airlines and research institutes will cover the remainder, a Sabena spokesman said.
Information will be collected on flights by Sabena, Lufthansa of Germany, Air France and Austrian Airlines to the United States, Africa, Latin America, Australia, Russia and northern Asia.

Five aircraft, one of them an Airbus company jet, will carry equipment collecting data on ozone concentrations at high altitudes, which will be processed in France before publication on the Internet. The Web address is not known at present.
Jets' kerosene-powered engines produce gases such as carbon dioxide and nitrous oxide which contribute to the formation of ozone and smog and to global warming.
Sabena said jet aircraft worldwide accounted for two or three percent of the total of nitrous oxide produced by man.
It said the results of the study would help aviation companies produce cleaner and more efficient engines.
The European Union has said it aims to cut carbon emissions from coal, oil and other fossil fuels by 15 percent from 1990 levels by 2010.
